thread:
IncidentBot: ALERT 2200 - node-gpu-12 /var/lib/kubelet > 94% disk usage, multiple pods evicted, 5xx spike on /generate and GPU container restarts. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

Sam (oncall): acked. looking. anyone oncall infra? @Priya?

Priya: i'm around. seeing evictions on node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-14. quick dump:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector=status.phase==Failed -o wide
NAME                       STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
modelcache-7b9f8           Evicted   0          2h    node-gpu-12
serve-runtime-5d4c3        CrashLoopBackOff  12  3h    node-gpu-12
chat-api-844d6             Running   0          30m   node-gpu-14 (tainted)
```

Priya: describe on one evicted:
```
Name:         modelcache-7b9f8
Reason:       Evicted
Message:      The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage.
```

Alex: looking at kubelet logs on node-gpu-12: repeated eviction manager entries + journal shows a backup job spiking /var/tmp/model-debug tar writes every 10m.

Alex: also saw GPU container startups failing immediately after eviction with error: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in runtime init in logs, which caused restart loops. stack: `Runtime failed to init cudax` then container OOM -> exit.

Maya: customer impact - Grace, heads up: some customers seeing higher 5xx on hosted endpoints, appears to be generation timeouts and immediate 503s when pods restart.

Grace (customer-ops): on it. triaging impacted customers. any ETA?

Sam (oncall): immediate plan: 1) reduce pressure on node-gpu-12 by draining non-critical pods, 2) free disk quickly (remove stale debug artifacts), 3) prevent backup job from running while we stabilize, 4) cordon node if we need to migrate.

Priya: i'm SSHing to node-gpu-12 now. listing top dirs:
```
root@node-gpu-12:~# du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/* | sort -h | tail -n 8
1.2G /var/lib/kubelet/pods/....../volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/modelcache
8.9G /var/tmp/model-debug-archive
12G /var/lib/docker/overlay2
```

Priya: there's a huge `/var/tmp/model-debug-archive` from a nightly debug exporter. i'm stopping the cron and cleaning the archive. removing oldest tarfiles now (will free ~9G).

Alex: i can trigger `kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for low-priority pods after we free ~10GB. want to avoid killing live model-serving pods mid-request.

Sam (oncall): hold on drain until Priya confirms free space. Maya, can you flip traffic to dedicated fallback region for high-volume customers? Use routing policy `region-fallback: true`.

Maya: doing a quick canary. shifting 30% of traffic for prod-realtime to us-west-2 (lower latency impact). sending deploy token to router. :white_check_mark:

Priya: deleted old tarballs, reclaimed 9.4G. `df -h /var/lib/kubelet` now shows 68% used.

Sam (oncall): proceed with drain of non-critical pods. Alex, start drain and watch for restarts.

Alex: draining non-critical pods...
```
$ kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30
WARNING: ignoring DaemonSet-managed pods: kube-proxy, node-exporter
evicting pod modelcache-7b9f8... evicted
evicting pod debug-runner-2... deleted
```

Alex: model-serving pod `serve-runtime-5d4c3` restarted after eviction and initially failed with CUDA OOM, but subsequent restarts succeeded once disk pressure cleared. logs:
```
E runtime: failed to init cuda: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY allocating 1.2GiB
I runtime: fallback to host-caching; resumed map
I serve: model loaded, ready
```

Priya: i also found `/var/log/serve-runtime/debug.log` is set to DEBUG and rotates weekly — huge log churn. set to INFO for now.

Sam (oncall): making temporary mitigation checklist:
- stop debug exporter cron (disabled)
- rotate and truncate debug logs to free space
- set log level INFO on serve-runtime pods via `kubectl set env` for the deploy
- cordon node-gpu-12 to prevent scheduling until K8s frees/reclaims
- patch backup job to include retention and size cap

Maya: doing `kubectl set env deployment/serve-runtime LOG_LEVEL=INFO -n inference` now.

Priya: cordoned node-gpu-12. marking as unschedulable.

Grace (customer-ops): messaging to impacted customers prepared: short notice "transient errors" with timeline, folks can DM for logs. i have list of customers with >1% error rate increase.

Sam (oncall): handoff - i'm 20m out. @Maya will take incident lead. next_oncall should be Maya. I'll leave postmortem notes in incident doc.

Maya: i'll take it. capturing action items and will run followups:
- add disk-space alert threshold earlier (85%)
- set ephemeral-storage requests for debug jobs
- alter cron to push debug artifacts to S3 rather than node-local
- add preemptive evict policy for local-empty-dir heavy pods

Alex: filing infra ticket INF-3421 to add size cap + retention, and INF-3422 to add pre-delete hooks for modelcache eviction to gracefully flush KV cache.

Sam (oncall): summary: root cause = debug exporter + oversized local archives filled /var/tmp -> kubelet eviction -> modelcache pods evicted -> serve-runtime restarts caused CUDA init OOMs during restart windows -> customer 5xx spike. Mitigation executed: cleaned archives, rotated logs, drained noncritical pods, cordoned node, shifted partial traffic.

Maya: timeline and mitigation steps will go to postmortem. assigning owners: Priya (cleanup + cron patch), Alex (drain automation + ticket), Grace (customer followups), Sam (postmortem draft).

Alex: filing infra ticket INF-3421 to add size cap + retention, and INF-3422 to add pre-delete hooks for modelcache eviction to gracefully flush KV cache.

Mitigation executed: cleaned archives, rotated logs, drained noncritical pods, cordoned node, shifted partial traffic.

Grace (customer-ops): I've sent initial customer notice and will follow up after postmortem.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE 2200 -> Status: mitigated (node stabilized, traffic normalizing). Keep thread for runbook follow-ups.

Sam (oncall): thanks team. leaving formal handoff. Maya, you're owner.

Maya: taking over, i'll post an interim retrospective tomorrow and schedule postmortem sync. :coffee:

(End of thread)
